source_refs.quoted_text:
def build_report(counts):
    planned = counts["planned"]
    retained = counts["retained"]
    removed = counts["removed"]
    events = counts["events"]
    rate = ratio(events, planned, "0.0001")
    pct = percentage(events, planned, "0.01")

evidence.description: The scope section explicitly bounds the claim as a lower bound on the planned-set fraction and disclaims any retained-subset-conditional rate.

source_refs.quoted_text:
## Scope of the claim
The reported rate uses the complete planned set of 40 light curves as its
exposure denominator, matching the declared scientific target. The 8 removed
light curves contribute to the denominator and contribute zero detected
flares, because no flare determination was possible for them. The rate is
therefore a lower bound on the flare-positive fraction of the planned set:
it is the fraction of planned light curves that were both screened in and
flare-positive. No claim is made about the flare status of the removed
light curves, and no rate conditional on the retained subset is reported here.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to establish that the issue is present by checking whether the selected result's denominator is the retained subset (32) while the claim targets the planned set (40). It is not: I recounted the data (40 rows total, 32 with flare determinations 0/1, 12 with flare_detected=1, 8 NA rows) and verified 12/40 = 0.3000 as reported, and verified the code passes counts['planned'] to the ratio. I also tried to construe the treatment of the 8 NA units as a hidden subset substitution, but the report explicitly discloses this treatment and bounds the claim as a lower bound on the planned-set fraction, so no retained-subset rate is presented for the complete domain.
